title: The page needs a language attribute
summary: The html element has no lang attribute, so screen readers guess the language. Add lang="en", or the right code for your page.
problem: The <html> element has no lang attribute. Browsers and assistive technology then cannot tell what language the page is written in, and have to guess.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users, whose software picks a voice and pronunciation rules from the page language. A wrong guess makes English read with a foreign accent, or the other way round. Translation tools and spell checkers rely on it too.
whyItMatters: Speech that is mispronounced is hard to follow and tiring to listen to. This is a WCAG 3.1.1 failure at Level A, the baseline that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
steps: Open the template or theme file that prints the opening <html> tag.
Add a lang attribute with the main language of the page, such as lang="en" for English or lang="fr" for French.
Use a valid language code, with a region only if it matters, such as en-GB.
If your site has several languages, set the code per page rather than hard-coding one.

howToCheck: View the page source and look at the opening <html> tag. It should contain lang with a language code. The browser developer tools also show it in the Elements panel.

platformNotes.note: Themes normally print lang with the language_attributes() function in header.php. The site language is set under Settings, General, Site Language.
